meta.subtitle: AI-driven growth is real, but a convertible-funded balance sheet, non-GAAP-based multiples and cycle risk leave the reward/risk short of a BUY

analystSentiment.commentary:
We rate Advanced Energy a HOLD with a $290–$410 target range over a 12-month horizon. The business is doing well on the company's own numbers: second-quarter 2026 revenue rose {+ 30% year over year +} and came in above the high end of guidance, according to the August 3, 2026 earnings release.

Our hesitation is about price. The forward multiples rest on consensus earnings that exclude items GAAP results carry (see Valuation), the share count is still absorbing the convertible notes (see Risks), and the stock trades well below its 52-week high (see Valuation). The company's cyclical history (see Financials) means a Bear case deserves real weight.

The scenario math derives HOLD: expected upside clears the BUY bar, but reward/risk does not. We would rather see the third-quarter results and the post-redemption share count than pay for the Street's path in advance.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Advanced Energy Industries, Inc. provides precision power conversion, measurement, and control solutions. Its plasma power products serve semiconductor and thin film plasma processes such as dry etch and deposition, and its high and low voltage power products go into semiconductor equipment, data center computing, industrial production, medical and life science equipment, networking, and telecommunications. It also sells sensing, controls and instrumentation products and a repair, calibration and refurbishment service business.

The company operates as a single segment of power electronics conversion products, sold into four markets: Semiconductor Equipment, Data Center Computing, Industrial and Medical, and Telecom and Networking. It sells to OEMs, distributors and end customers. The company was incorporated in 1981 and is headquartered in Denver, Colorado.

FY25 revenue was $1.8B, up 21.4%. In our reading, Advanced Energy is a cyclical equipment supplier whose current growth comes mainly from AI-related demand (see Growth).

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body:
Advanced Energy is executing well: revenue growth has accelerated, gross margin has stepped up, and third-quarter guidance points higher again (see Financials). After the May 2026 convertible refinancing, it still holds more cash than debt.

The price already reflects much of this. At $297.29 the stock trades on a high trailing GAAP multiple, and its forward multiples look reasonable only on the earnings basis discussed in Valuation. The convertible notes add potential shares (see Risks), and the business has turned down sharply before (see Financials).

We weight a Base case built on FY27E consensus EPS most heavily, but a credible Bear case keeps reward/risk below the BUY threshold. HOLD.

catalysts: Third-quarter 2026 results, measured against the guidance set out in Financials.
Data Center Computing: the 10-Q expects AI-driven demand and adoption of next generation high power solutions to support growth in the remainder of 2026 (see Growth).
Semiconductor Equipment: the company expects current market conditions to continue in the remainder of the year (see Growth).
The third-quarter 10-Q's diluted share count, which will show the effect of the 2028 Notes redemption that was set for September 23, 2026; the outcome is not yet in the sources (see Financials).
risks: Cyclicality: revenue fell in both FY23 and FY24 before recovering (see Financials).
Dilution from the convertible notes, which also widens the gap between GAAP and non-GAAP earnings (see Risks).
A sharp, unexplained fall from the 52-week high (see Valuation).
Component lead times and prices are rising with AI-related demand, which the 10-Q says could become material (see Risks).

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary:
The annual record shows a cyclical business. Revenue fell {- 10.3% -} in FY23 and {- 10.5% -} in FY24, and operating margin dropped to 2.5% in FY24 before recovering to 9.3% in FY25 on revenue growth of {+ 21.4% +}. Diluted EPS fell from $5.29 in FY22 to $1.43 in FY24. Gross margin held in a narrow band, from 35.7% to 37.7%, across FY21–FY25. That downturn is the reference point for our Bear weight and our moat rating.

The second quarter of 2026 moved well above that band. Revenue was $574.1M against $441.5M a year earlier, gross margin was 41.1% against 37.0%, and operating income was $95.1M against $31.6M. The end-market drivers are covered in Growth.

GAAP and non-GAAP earnings diverge sharply. GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations was $1.29, against $0.67 a year earlier, and included $31.8 million, or $0.75 per diluted share, of inducement costs on the partial conversion of the 2028 notes. Non-GAAP EPS was $2.74. Diluted weighted-average shares were 42.3 million, against 37.8 million a year earlier and 42.2 million in Q1 2026.

The August 3, 2026 release guides third-quarter 2026 revenue to $640 million +/- $20 million, GAAP EPS from continuing operations to $2.38 +/- $0.25 and non-GAAP EPS to $3.00 +/- $0.25. That guidance implies another sequential step up. We think the margin improvement is real, though GAAP earnings remain well below the non-GAAP figures.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary:
At December 31, 2025, total debt of $567.5M sat entirely in current debt, which is why the FY25 current ratio was only 1.59. Net debt was negative, a net cash position of $223.7M, so the company held more cash than debt before it refinanced.

On May 18, 2026, the company issued $1.15 billion of 0% Convertible Notes due 2031 and received net proceeds of approximately $1,128.1 million. At the same time it exchanged approximately $438.3 million principal of its 2.5% 2028 Notes for approximately $442.4 million in cash and approximately 2.0 million shares. The 10-Q says the company intends to use the remaining net proceeds for general corporate purposes and debt repayment.

At June 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents were $1,396.5 million, current debt was $135.6 million and long-term debt was $1,128.6 million. Cash still exceeded total debt, though by a narrower margin than at year-end, and most of the debt now sits in the zero-coupon 2031 Notes. The TTM current ratio is 3.79. Inventories rose to $538.1 million from $411.2 million at year-end, which fits the higher revenue run rate but adds exposure if demand turns.

On June 12, 2026, the company called the remaining $136.7 million of 2028 Notes for redemption on September 23, 2026. The conversion price was approximately $137.46, and the company elected to settle principal in cash and the remainder in shares. That date has passed, but the outcome is not in the sources. Liquidity is strong; the share-count consequences are discussed in Risks.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary:
Cash generation has trailed earnings growth because of capacity spending. FY25 free cash flow was $125.9M, a 7.0% FCF margin, after capital expenditure of $107.4M. The 2026 proxy statement reports FY2025 operating cash flow from continuing operations of $235 million. FCF margin has ranged between 5.0% and 8.9% over FY21–FY25, which is modest for a stock valued at these multiples.

The second quarter of 2026 was stronger: the release reports $86 million of cash flow from continuing operations and $4.1 million of quarterly dividends. The 10-K says the company accelerated investments in capacity to meet Data Center Computing demand, so we do not expect capital spending to fall soon.

Shareholder returns are small. FY25 share repurchases were $30.2M and dividends paid were $15.6M, and the dividend yield is 0.13%. The TTM FCF yield of 0.7% means the shares are priced on future growth, not current cash.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
On trailing figures the stock is expensive: P/E (TTM) is 55.3x, EV/EBITDA (TTM) is 35.5x and P/S is 5.8x. The trailing P/E is based on GAAP earnings, which include the inducement costs described in Financials.

The forward multiples look much lower, with two caveats. First, the vendor's "NTM" P/E of 26.4x matches the price over FY26E EPS of $11.24, so it is in effect a current-year multiple. On FY27E EPS of $15.34 the multiple is ~19.4x. Second, consensus EPS is very likely non-GAAP: FY26E sits far above FY25 GAAP diluted EPS of $3.84 and in line with the company's non-GAAP run rate. These forward multiples should not be read as GAAP multiples.

The Street is bullish. Eleven of 12 analysts rate the stock a Buy and one a Hold, with a consensus target of $429.08, a median of $412.50 and a range of $370.00–$535.00. No peer multiples were available (peers are pending a peer data source), so we make no peer comparison.

The price matters as much as the multiple. At $297.29 the stock sits well below its 52-week high of $397.44 and well above its low of $169.36. None of the sources explains the fall from the high, so we read it as a sign that the market may be questioning either the durability of AI-related demand or the multiple, not as a free discount.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Data Center Computing and Semiconductor Equipment demand both hold through 2027, FY27E consensus EPS is delivered, and the market pays close to the Street's consensus target of $429.08.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: FY27E EPS of $15.34 comes through on the non-GAAP basis, and the market values it at a multiple roughly midway between today's ~19.4x on FY27E and the 26.4x it pays on FY26E. The result sits below the Street low target of $370.00.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Growth stalls: AI-related and semiconductor equipment orders slow, FY27 earnings get no higher than FY26E EPS of $11.24, and the market pays only the lower FY27E-based multiple named in Base.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Our horizon is 12 months. The Base case carries the most weight because second-quarter results and third-quarter guidance (see Financials) support the consensus growth path. We still value FY27E earnings below the multiple the market now pays on FY26E, because the earnings basis and the rising share count both work against per-share value.

The Bull case takes the Street at its word. We give it a 25% weight, below the Base, because the consensus target assumes the stock regains and passes its 52-week high.

The Bear case gets a 30% weight. It is a growth stall rather than a repeat of the last downturn: earnings flatten at the FY26E level and the multiple compresses. Order visibility is limited (see Risks), and the fall from the 52-week high suggests the market may already be questioning the multiple.

The weighted result clears the BUY threshold on expected upside but falls short on reward/risk, so the derived label is HOLD. The deciding split is Bear against Base. Moving weight from Bear to Base would push the call toward BUY, and the strength of the second quarter argues for that. We keep the Bear weight because a downturn deeper than our Bear, like the one in Financials, remains possible and is not priced in any scenario. The call is close on expected upside and less close on reward/risk.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Advanced Energy reports a single segment of power electronics conversion products, so no segment split is reported below the consolidated total. Its products and end markets are described in the company overview. The single segment does not mean a single competitive position: each market has its own customers and design cycles, so the moat factors below apply unevenly across the business.

moatFactors.name: Design-win incumbency
moatFactors.body: The 10-K says new products designed for capital equipment manufacturers typically have a lifespan of many years, and the company works with customers early in their design cycles. A win can therefore earn revenue for years. The same filing says design windows may be narrow, that there is no assurance of new wins, and that the company may not maintain single source status. Incumbency helps, but it is re-contested with every equipment generation.

moatFactors.name: End-market diversification
moatFactors.body: Selling into four markets lets growth in one offset weakness in another; the 2026 proxy reports Data Center Computing growth in 2025 while Industrial and Medical declined. The protection is partial: the last downturn (see Financials) shows that diversification softens the cycle without removing it.

moatFactors.name: Manufacturing footprint
moatFactors.body: The 2026 proxy says the company exited its last factory in China during 2025 while adding capacity in the Philippines and Mexico. Separately, it says the company "effectively managed the impact of tariffs" that year. We think the move may reduce tariff exposure, but the proxy does not link the two. The 10-Q lists the scaling of capacity and timely customer qualification of new manufacturing lines as risks, so the footprint is still being built out.

businessMoat.durability:
We rate the moat NARROW. Gross margin held its narrow FY21–FY25 band through the last downturn (see Financials), which suggests some pricing resilience. Customers choose the products on power conversion efficiency, power density, low noise and the ability to tailor solutions, according to the 10-Q, and those are engineering attributes that take time to match.

The moat is not wide. The 10-Q lists pricing pressure from customers and competitors among its risks, and the 10-K says competitors may be more successful in implementing an AI strategy. Limited order visibility (see Risks) means the advantage has to be re-earned with each design cycle. The current margin expansion may owe as much to strong demand as to durable advantage, and we would want to see it hold through a softer quarter before rating the moat higher.

points: Data Center Computing is the main growth driver on the figures available. The 2026 proxy reports that this market's revenue grew 107% in 2025 to $587 million, on demand from hyperscale customers for new AI data center power solutions. The 10-Q says revenue rose again in 2026's first half compared with a year earlier, due to increased AI investment by leading hyperscale customers, and expects the trend to continue along with adoption of next generation high power solutions. The counterweight is dependence on the AI spending of those customers.

Semiconductor Equipment growth accelerated. The 2026 proxy reports 2025 Semiconductor revenue of $840 million, up 6%, and the August 2026 release says Semiconductor revenue grew 33% year over year in the second quarter of 2026. The 10-Q ties this to demand for leading-edge logic and memory used in AI applications and expects these conditions to continue in the remainder of the year. The 10-K says several of the markets in which the company competes are highly cyclical, so we treat this acceleration as cycle-dependent.

Industrial and Medical is recovering. The 2026 proxy says revenue in this market fell 11% for 2025, but it bottomed in Q1 2025, rose sequentially each quarter and returned to year-over-year growth by Q4. The 10-Q says the company believes demand has returned to normalized levels, and it expects demand to continue to improve in the remainder of 2026. This market depends less on AI spending, which makes it a useful offset if that spending slows.

Telecom and Networking remained stable in 2026's first half, with growth driven mainly by AI-related applications, according to the 10-Q. We treat it as a steady contributor rather than a driver of the thesis.

Consensus expects FY26E revenue of ~$2.4B (+35%) and FY27E revenue of $3B. The company's own guidance supports the near term, but the 10-K warns that if the company has not accurately assessed the magnitude or sustainability of AI-driven demand, its results of operations could be adversely impacted.

management.leadership:
The 2026 proxy statement, filed March 26, 2026, names Stephen Kelley as President and Chief Executive Officer and Paul Oldham as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. The other named executive officers for 2025 were Eduardo Bernal Acebedo (Chief Operations Officer), Elizabeth Vonne (General Counsel & Corporate Secretary) and John Donaghey (Chief Commercial Officer).

The execution record in the sources is good. Second-quarter 2026 results exceeded guidance (see Financials), and the manufacturing moves out of China were completed during 2025. The test ahead is whether the team can scale capacity for Data Center Computing without the forecasting and inventory problems the 10-K flags as risks.
management.capitalAllocation:
The main capital decision of 2026 was the convertible refinancing described in Financials, which retired most of the 2.5% 2028 Notes and called the rest; the company still holds more cash than debt. Its cost is potential dilution, covered in Risks.

Capital spending is going into capacity for AI-related demand, which we think is the right priority given the growth in Data Center Computing. Repurchases and dividends are small relative to the market value (see Financials). The large cash balance leaves open whether it will fund acquisitions; the 10-Q lists acquisition integration among its risks. We view the allocation as reasonable, and we want to see how much of the cash is put to work.
management.governance:
Governance information comes from the 2026 proxy statement, filed March 26, 2026, and the excerpt is truncated, so it does not cover board independence or committee composition. Grant H. Beard is Chairman of the Board and Stephen Kelley is Chief Executive Officer, so the two roles are held by different people.

The proxy says a majority of the named executive officers' 2025 target pay was performance-based, tied to financial and stock price performance under the 2025 short-term and long-term incentive plans. The August 2026 earnings release adds that management's incentive plans include certain non-GAAP measures as criteria. The excerpt does not show which measures the 2025 plans used, and how future awards treat convertible-related costs is a question for the next proxy. On what the excerpt shows, we see the pay structure as reasonably aligned with outside holders.
management.insiderOwnership:
As of March 1, 2026, the proxy reports that all executive officers and directors as a group (14 persons) beneficially owned 476,577 shares, or 1.3% of the 37,848,305 shares then outstanding. The holders above five percent were BlackRock, Inc. at 14.6%, The Vanguard Group at 13.0% and FMR LLC at 5.2%, each based on Schedule 13G/A filings with older as-of dates: June 30, 2025 for BlackRock, December 31, 2024 for Vanguard and December 31, 2025 for FMR. No holder is near a majority, so no single shareholder controls the company.

Insider alignment therefore comes mainly through performance-based pay rather than ownership. The March 2026 share count also predates the shares issued in the May 2026 note exchange, and our current share figure is derived from market value and price rather than a reported count, so we do not read precision into it.

idiosyncratic: Convertible dilution. At the conversion price given in Financials, well below the current price, converted 2028 Notes add shares, and the 2031 Notes add further potential shares. The 10-Q also lists dilution and counterparty default risk related to the convertible debt, hedge, warrant and capped call transactions; the excerpt gives no terms for the hedges, so we cannot judge how much dilution they offset. The mechanism is a rising diluted share count that caps per-share growth. The third-quarter 10-Q will show the share count after the redemption.

Order visibility and customer concentration. The 10-K says sales are primarily made on a purchase order basis, the company generally does not have long-term purchase commitments, and customers may delay or cancel orders and may not be subject to cancellation penalties; the 10-Q lists concentration of the customer base as a risk. A pause by a few large customers could cut revenue quickly. The signal to track is inventory, which has already risen (see Financials), against the revenue run rate.

Supply and cost pressure. The 10-Q says AI-related demand is extending lead times and increasing prices of certain components, and that these factors, while not material this quarter, could become material. The 10-K adds that some supplier contracts require the company to purchase a specified number of components each quarter. The mechanism is margin squeeze or excess inventory, and a gross margin falling back from the second-quarter level (see Financials) would be an early sign.

Design-win and technology risk. The 10-K says competitors may develop more successful products with the aid of AI technology and that design windows may be narrow. Losing a platform at a large customer would hurt revenue for years. Adoption of the next generation high power solutions the 10-Q expects to support Data Center Computing growth is the test.
risks.systemic:
The 10-K says several of the markets in which the company competes are highly cyclical, with downturns characterized by diminished product demand, production overcapacity, high inventory levels and price erosion; the company's own experience of that is in Financials. Today the main systemic exposure is AI-related capital spending: both Semiconductor Equipment and Data Center Computing growth depend on it, so a broad slowdown in AI investment would hit two markets at once.

The 10-Q also cites tariffs and trade policy, geopolitical instability including the conflicts in the Middle East, volatility in energy markets and disruptions to global shipping. It says these were not material to results in the current quarter but could become material through higher energy and supply chain costs. Rates and inflation matter mainly through customers' access to capital and through the multiple the market will pay for growth. We see the AI capital-spending cycle as the risk that matters most.

body: HOLD, with a target range of $290–$410 over 12 months. Advanced Energy is growing quickly and its balance sheet is liquid, but the valuation already prices much of the consensus path (see Valuation) and the share count is still absorbing the convertible notes. Our scenarios give expected upside that clears the BUY bar but reward/risk that does not. The low end of the range sits below the current price, reflecting our Bear weight.

We would upgrade to BUY if third-quarter 2026 results land above the top of the guided revenue and non-GAAP EPS ranges (see Financials) and the post-redemption diluted share count shows dilution is contained, which would justify moving weight from Bear to Base. We would downgrade if third-quarter revenue falls below the bottom of the guided range or gross margin falls back toward its FY21–FY25 band, which would signal that the cycle is turning.
